title: The Analog Vault
desc: Lost recordings, contract wars, sampling lawsuits & studio mythology

questions.q: The 'loudness war' in music mastering peaked in 2008 with which Metallica album that fans petitioned to have remastered?
questions.a: Death Magnetic — the Guitar Hero version actually sounded better because it hadn't been brick-wall compressed

questions.q: Brian Wilson spent years and millions recording an album that was shelved as 'too ahead of its time'. What was it called and when did it finally get released?
questions.a: SMiLE — recorded 1966-67, officially released in 2011 (44 years later)

questions.q: The 'Amen break' is a 6-second drum loop from a 1969 B-side that became the backbone of jungle, drum & bass, and hip-hop. Who played it?
questions.a: Gregory Coleman of The Winstons, on the track 'Amen, Brother' — he died homeless and never received royalties

questions.q: Which rapper's debut album was recorded entirely on a prison-issued JPay tablet while serving time?
questions.a: This is a trick — while several rappers have recorded in prison, no major debut was made entirely on a JPay tablet. The question tests if you'll guess confidently

questions.q: Robert Johnson allegedly sold his soul to the devil at a crossroads in exchange for guitar mastery. Where is this crossroads supposedly located?
questions.a: The intersection of Highways 61 and 49 in Clarksdale, Mississippi (though historians debate the exact spot)

questions.q: Phil Spector's 'Wall of Sound' technique involved doing what unusual thing with the recording process?
questions.a: Having multiple musicians play the same parts simultaneously in a small echo chamber — layering identical performances for density

questions.q: What is 'brickwalling' in audio mastering, and why do audiophiles hate it?
questions.a: Compressing the dynamic range so everything is equally loud — it removes the quiet-to-loud contrast that gives music emotional impact

questions.q: Radiohead's 'Kid A' (2000) baffled fans by abandoning guitar rock. Which electronic artist was the primary influence Thom Yorke cited?
questions.a: Aphex Twin (Richard D. James) — Yorke also cited Warp Records and Autechre

questions.q: Which legendary Motown songwriter and producer was blind from birth and signed to the label at age 11?
questions.a: Stevie Wonder (Stevland Hardaway Judkins) — he signed in 1961

questions.q: The original master tapes for thousands of classic recordings were destroyed in a 2008 fire at Universal Studios. Name one artist whose masters were confirmed lost.
questions.a: Nirvana, Tupac, Elton John, Snoop Dogg, R.E.M., Sonic Youth, Beck, Nine Inch Nails — among many others
